title: Georgia Open Records Act Request: Draft ALPR Policy Described by the City Manager at the November 24, 2026 Council Meeting

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Georgia Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

At the November 24, 2026 City Council meeting, the City Manager said that he and the City Attorney would be finalizing “in the coming days” a specific policy governing automated license plate readers (ALPRs). The remark comes about 1 hour 46 minutes into the meeting recording.

Every draft or version of that ALPR policy that exists on the date of this request, in the form it was shared. This includes any version the City Manager’s Office or the City Attorney’s Office sent to the Police Department, Procurement, or the Mayor and Aldermen. If a draft has tracked changes or comments, please send it with them visible.
Any model policy, template, or example policy from another city, a state agency, a professional association, or a vendor (including Flock Safety, Axon, and Motorola Solutions) that the City received or used while preparing the draft.
Email metadata only (sender, all recipients including cc and bcc, subject line, and date and time) for any email to or from the City Manager’s Office or the City Attorney’s Office, from October 1, 2026 through the date of this request, that attached or sent a draft ALPR policy or a model policy covered by items 1 and 2.
If the policy has been signed, adopted, or issued by the time you process this request, the final version. If it has not, please tell me in writing and I will request the final version separately.

These records are likely held by the City Manager’s Office and the City Attorney’s Office. Copies may also be with the Police Department or Procurement, so please search each. If any record is withheld in whole or in part, please tell me the specific legal authority by Code section, subsection, and paragraph, as O.C.G.A. § 50-18-71(d) provides, and release the rest. Please also list each withheld record by date, author, and type, so I can tell what was held back.

I would like item 1 first. If items 2 or 3 will take longer or cost more, please send item 1 and give me the timeline and estimate for the rest. I am glad to narrow them. For any item where no record exists, please tell me in writing. I do not authorize any work that would exceed $25 until I have approved the estimate.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Ethan Watters
